abstract: Hypertext and hypermedia present information in a form very different to the conventional printed page-the details of the method are described. These ideas are related to the future of publishing. Collaborative documents and communal knowledge bases are hypermedia applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Database structure at the Press Association
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Large Databases in Press and Publishing: The Present and the Future
abstract: The Press Association covers news and comments about every aspect of life from politics, finance, sports, general news to domestic products. In terms of volume and type of information, this is a large amount of data to collect and store in an organised manner. The data is handled by a large number of people of different backgrounds and interests and is processed and tailored as required for different types of readers and research. To accomplish these requirements and maintain data consistency, integrity and security, database management has been the main tool in PA's everyday operation. The PA database management system consists of several sub-systems which are responsible for processing each individual database. Some of these are described briefly: editorial system, sports system, elections system, TV programmes system, graphic system and message switch and networks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Large Databases in Press and Publishing: The Present and the Future
abstract: Technology for access and storage of unstructured information is discussed. The author looks at various text input methods including OCR and ICR and image processing techniques-image compression standards are outlined. Translation of an image into a WP document is considered. Imaging systems can be classified as: electronic filing cabinet, integrate with other data and integrate into business. The 2 main methods for supporting images inside a database are given. Various specific multi-media databases for handling unstructured text, image and voice data are discussed and developments in this area are identified.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: NRT (News Retrieval Tool): a user's guide
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Large Databases in Press and Publishing: The Present and the Future
abstract: NRT, the News Retrieval Tool is the result of a six month research project between Glasgow University and the Financial Times. The aim of the project was to improve the retrieval methods and the user interface of the existing Profile retrieval service. The test system that has been built by the project consists of two computers, a Macintosh and the Profile search engine, communicating over a phone line. The Profile computer, using a new set of search algorithms developed by the project, searches a store of the 1989 articles of the Financial Times. The Macintosh runs a graphical user interface that presents an easy to use front end to the remote Profile search engine. The author explains how to perform and control searches, how to browse and how to construct a good query.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Large Databases in Press and Publishing: The Present and the Future
abstract: A definition of the database is given. The author goes on to discuss his own company's (Financial Times newspaper) involvement in the industry. He looks at the political climate, markets and legal issues. The importance of the newspaper as a source and the use of database in this role are discussed: Various aspects of the use of online databases and electronic publishing by newspaper companies are outlined, e.g., competitive advantage, price and value role of the information professional and quality assurance. The use of new media in newspapers is also discussed, including CD-ROM variants, fax and broadcast.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
